name: OpenSpiel Game-Playing Benchmark
description: We present a new general board game (GBG) playing and learning framework. GBG defines the common interfaces for board games, game states and their AI agents. It allows one to run competitions of different agents on different games. It standardizes those parts of board game playing and learning that otherwise would be tedious and repetitive parts in coding. GBG is suitable for arbitrary 1-, 2-, ..., N-player board games. It makes a generic TD($λ$)-n-tuple agent for the first time available to arbitrary games. On various games, TD($λ$)-n-tuple is found to be superior to other generic agents like MCTS. GBG aims at the educational perspective, where it helps students to start faster in the area of game learning. GBG aims as well at the research perspective by collecting a growing set of games and AI agents to assess their strengths and generalization capabilities in meaningful competitions. Initial successful educational and research results are reported.
evaluation_method: Win rate, game outcome statistics, exploitability for imperfect-information games, and average payoff or Elo-style ratings depending on the game.
typical_sota_score: varies widely by game and setting; no single unified SOTA — e.g., >90% win rate for strong agents in many solved perfect-information board games, exploitability reported as very low (e.g., <0.01) for top solvers on some imperfect-information benchmarks; overall game- and metric-dependent
notes: More of a framework than a single fixed leaderboard task; evaluation depends strongly on the chosen game and protocol.
